name: What hidden issues are most common in older Los Angeles homes during remodeling?

mainEntity.name: What hidden issues are most common in older Los Angeles homes during remodeling?
mainEntity.text: What hidden issues are most common in older Los Angeles homes during remodeling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes often look straightforward until demolition exposes what is behind the walls. The most common surprises are outdated electrical systems, galvanized or deteriorated plumbing, moisture damage, dry rot, termite damage, and framing that no longer meets current expectations. Some homes also reveal unpermitted alterations from prior owners, which can complicate permitting and inspections. Hillside and coastal homes may face additional concerns such as drainage problems, settlement, or corrosion. Because these issues are hard to see upfront, a good remodel budget should include contingency, and the contract should explain how hidden conditions will be documented and priced. It is also smart to ask whether the contractor has experience with homes of similar age and construction type. If a remodel is being planned in neighborhoods with older housing stock like Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, or North Hollywood, hidden conditions should be expected rather than treated as rare events. The best protection is a detailed preconstruction review and a contractor who knows how to pivot without derailing the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden issues include outdated wiring, old plumbing, water damage, dry rot, foundation movement, and framing problems. These often appear after demolition and can change both the budget and timeline.
